note: Round-3 judged vocabulary (4+8+16 papers). Types name the ROLE in the argument; technique, material, quantity, direction, mechanism class and basis go in attrs. OBS subtypes name what feature of the data is read; figure form is the modality field, data origin the provenance field. Node field spine marks the primary line of argument. From v03 the merge phase is open: see usage (r01-r03 counts after renames) and rounds/r03/judge.md.

HYP.definition: Motivation, knowledge gap, or hypothesis that the work sets out to test

HYP/gap.definition: Something is unknown, unmeasured, unexplained or contradictory in the literature; closing it yields knowledge. Kind (unobserved regime, unexplained effect, conflicting reports) in attrs.gap_kind
HYP/gap.example: Kinetics of the alpha-to-beta transformation in Ti at ns time scales have never been measured directly

HYP/need.definition: An application or societal requirement (property level, cost, sustainability, safety) that current materials fail to meet; closing it yields a better material
HYP/need.example: Mg alloy AZ91 lacks creep resistance above 150 C; petroleum polyols and xylene should be replaced

HYP/hypothesis.definition: A testable expectation or proposed strategy: doing X should produce Y. The work later confirms, refutes or qualifies it
HYP/hypothesis.example: Adding SiC particles should raise the strength and creep resistance of the Mg matrix

DES.definition: Choice of material system, composition, architecture, route or experiment, made for a stated reason

DES/base_system.definition: Choice of the host/base material or starting feedstock, with the reason (cost, renewability, known structure, availability)
DES/base_system.example: Use non-edible karanja oil as the polyol feedstock; choose AZ91 as matrix

DES/modification.definition: Choice to add or substitute a constituent into a base (dopant, alloying element, reinforcement, filler, co-monomer, additive). Site, amount and intended role in attrs. Verification of incorporation follows
DES/modification.example: Substitute Cr3+ on the Ti4+ site because the ionic radii match

DES/architecture.definition: A priori choice of a geometric or spatial target to be built: pore/channel lattice, external shape, strut network (incl. image-derived biomimetic), layer stacking, core-shell or graded/zoned placement of constituents. Geometry source and dimensions in attrs. A design-fidelity check (mm_op match_to_design) follows
DES/architecture.example: 8 mm cylinders with orthogonal 500-800 um channels at 50% designed pore volume

DES/route.definition: Choice of processing route, technique or auxiliary (solvent, catalyst, atmosphere) justified against a baseline or a structural target
DES/route.example: Replace xylene with bio-derived dipentene as coating solvent

DES/method.definition: Choice of characterization/test method, specimen geometry or sampling protocol because it enables or validates a measurement. Aspect (technique | specimen | sampling) in attrs. May sit on the spine only when the method itself is a headline contribution; it then reaches the claim it makes measurable by realizes
DES/method.example: Use single-shot dynamic TEM on 75 nm films, each shot on a fresh region

DES/variable_sweep.definition: The controlled variable(s) and levels that form the comparison axis of the study. Variable and levels in attrs
DES/variable_sweep.example: Reinforcement content 0-25 wt% in 5 wt% steps

DES/down_select.definition: A design decision made after, and because of, an observation, a screen or a weighed claim (trade-off, ranking): feedback edge OBS/PRP/PRF/MEC -> DES via motivates. Screen-then-choose papers put it on the spine
DES/down_select.example: IPDI chosen as the diisocyanate after the coating-quality screen

PRC.definition: A processing act or condition applied to make, shape or modify the material

PRC/synthesis.definition: A chemical or physical reaction or assembly step that turns precursors into the target compound, phase, polymer or supramolecular/colloidal object (solid-state reaction, sol-gel incl. the calcination that converts the gel/precursor, co-precipitation, polymerisation, functionalisation, self-assembly of micelles/vesicles/nanoparticles in dispersion). Boundary: if the input is not yet the target compound (precursor, gel, hydroxide, salt, mixed oxides) the step is synthesis even if it is thermal. Reactive consolidation (reactive hot pressing/SPS, SHS) that converts and densifies in one act is ONE synthesis node with attrs.concurrent_forming=true
PRC/synthesis.example: Epoxidise oil C=C bonds with H2O2 over Amberlyst 15; reactive hot pressing of ZrB2+ZrSi2+C at 1550 C

PRC/forming.definition: Turning feedstock (powder, melt, solution, sol, pellets) into a bulk body or a designed shape: casting (incl. into molds/templates), sintering/hot pressing/SPS of the made compound, powder compaction, extrusion or moulding of powder/melt/polymer feedstock, additive manufacturing, composite mixing-and-solidification, in-situ gelation/solidification in a mould or on site, and lithographic or subtractive patterning (photolithography + etching, laser ablation) of a deposited film into a designed geometry incl. transfer printing. Boundaries: thermomechanical working of an already-made solid body (hot extrusion of a cast billet, rolling, forging, ECAP) is PRC/treatment; reactive consolidation is PRC/synthesis; joining of pre-made bodies is PRC/joining
PRC/forming.example: Spark plasma sintering of powders into >96% dense pellets; photolithographic etching of PZT film into ribbon networks

PRC/deposition.definition: Applying material onto a substrate as film, coating or layer (PVD, CVD, evaporation, spin/bar coating, electrodeposition, spraying, self-assembly of a colloidal/molecular film on the substrate)
PRC/deposition.example: Bar-coat 120 um films on steel panels

PRC/joining.definition: Joining two or more pre-made bodies into one assembly across a new interface: diffusion bonding, brazing, welding, transient-liquid-phase and adhesive bonding. The product is a joint; interface reaction layers, bond soundness and joint (assembly) properties with attrs.object='joint' follow
PRC/joining.example: Vacuum diffusion bonding of EHEA and TiAl blocks at 900-1000 C

PRC/treatment.definition: Modifying the structure of an already-made material of the target compound without changing what compound it is: annealing, ageing, solution treatment, quenching, curing of a made polymer, thermomechanical working of a made solid body (rolling, forging, ECAP, hot extrusion of a cast billet), electropulsing, surface or irradiation treatment applied as part of making the material to be used, and size reduction/classification of a made powder (milling, grinding, sieve or centrifugal classification, spray drying). Before/after comparison follows. Boundary: calcination of an as-made precursor/gel is PRC/synthesis; exposure that simulates service or probes response is PRC/stimulus
PRC/treatment.example: Solution treatment at 520 C then ageing at 180 C; hot extrusion of cast Mg-Li billets; wet milling of Si powder to d50 = 62 nm

PRC/stimulus.definition: An external perturbation or exposure (thermal pulse or ageing test, load, field, electrochemical bias or cycling, corrosive/biological environment, irradiation) whose effect IS the object of study: it probes or tests a finished material, in situ or post-mortem, and is not part of making the material to be used
PRC/stimulus.example: Single 12 ns laser pulse heats the film at 1e11 K/s during pump-probe imaging

OBS.definition: A readout from a measurement or computation, before interpretation. Carries modality, provenance and (if it has figs) image_support. Subtypes name WHAT FEATURE OF THE DATA IS READ; technique goes in attrs, figure form in modality

OBS/signal.definition: Readouts of discrete features (peaks, bands, reflections, edges, steps, maxima, crossings) of a spectrum, pattern, scan, dispersion diagram or a distribution over a non-spatial coordinate (pole figure, misorientation histogram peak)

OBS/signal/reference_match.definition: The whole measured pattern/spectrum is judged to coincide (or not) with a reference: parent sample, standard, database card or simulation
OBS/signal/reference_match.example: Doped XRD patterns reproduce the undoped reflections, no extra peaks

OBS/signal/feature_assignment.definition: Individual features are assigned to origins: reflections indexed to phases, bands to functional groups, NMR signals to sites, DTG/DSC steps to processes
OBS/signal/feature_assignment.example: Six 1H NMR signals a-f mapped onto sites of the drawn polyol structure

OBS/signal/feature_presence.definition: A feature appears or disappears between samples, stages or times (qualitative presence/absence)
OBS/signal/feature_presence.example: NCO band at 2257 cm-1 absent after urethane formation

OBS/signal/feature_shift.definition: A feature's position read relative to a reference: moving across a series or condition (aspect=shift), or offset/overlapping with a feature of another species or quantity on the same axis (aspect=overlap: donor emission vs acceptor absorption, emission vs photonic stopband or plasmon resonance, absorption edge vs source spectrum, band-edge alignment). Direction, magnitude and reference feature in attrs
OBS/signal/feature_shift.example: (0 0 10) reflection shifts to higher 2theta with Cr content; coumarin emission (505 nm) overlaps closed-form BP-BTE absorption (590 nm)

OBS/signal/feature_quantification.definition: Feature intensity, area or width read as a measure of an amount or degree, qualitatively (grows, broadens, fades) or converted to a number: phase fraction, degree of conversion, concentration, crystallite size or strain from broadening, coordination from shell magnitude, texture strength from pole-figure maxima
OBS/signal/feature_quantification.example: Integrated difference-pattern intensities give 26 +/- 5% beta phase

OBS/response.definition: Readouts of a measured or computed quantity as a function of a variable or condition, or over an ensemble of samples, sites or configurations

OBS/response/trend.definition: How a quantity changes with a varied variable (design variable, temperature, time, stress): direction, monotonicity, ranking, saturation in attrs
OBS/response/trend.example: Yield strength rises monotonically with SiCp content; beta fraction vs log time is sigmoidal

OBS/response/characteristic_value.definition: A defined point or level read from a curve, test or table: onset, peak, step, minimum, value at a condition, standard-test rating, or a single summary statistic (mean, d50) when the spread itself is not argued
OBS/response/characteristic_value.example: Three TGA mass-loss steps at 184-355, 342-480, 480-655 C; pencil hardness 4H

OBS/response/fitted_parameter.definition: A parameter obtained by fitting a functional form or model to data: exponent, slope, activation energy, threshold, rate constant
OBS/response/fitted_parameter.example: Apparent stress exponent n = 7.2-8.9 from log-log creep rate vs stress

OBS/response/distribution.definition: The spread and shape of a non-imaged quantity sampled over an ensemble (computed sites/configurations, test specimens, particles in a light-scattering measurement, indents) read as the result: range, width, tails, multimodality, per-class offsets, or overlap of two distributions. Quantity and ensemble in attrs. Next: a heterogeneity/local-environment attribution, a reliability (Weibull) argument or an overlap argument that a single value cannot license. Boundaries: statistics of imaged features are OBS/morphology/feature_metric; peaks of orientation/misorientation distributions are OBS/signal; a single statistic whose spread is not argued is characteristic_value
OBS/response/distribution.example: Vacancy formation energies over all SQS sites span 2.45-3.94 eV (spread 1.49 eV); DLS size distribution narrow, mode ~21 nm

OBS/response/component_partition.definition: A total response shown together with its separated contributions, so the dominant term can be read
OBS/response/component_partition.example: Total and electronic thermal conductivity plotted on shared axes

OBS/response/regime_map.definition: Boundaries between states or regimes in a space of two or more conditions: TTT/CCT, phase diagram, processing or deformation-mechanism map, stability window
OBS/response/regime_map.example: Experimental TTT diagram from 10/50/90% transformation times

OBS/morphology.definition: Readouts of spatial/visual content of an image or map (micrograph, photograph, element map, tomogram)

OBS/morphology/appearance.definition: Qualitative reading of what features look like: shape, surface/fracture features, interface sharpness, defects, colour, gloss, uniformity of a film. Object imaged in attrs.object
OBS/morphology/appearance.example: Fracture surface shows dimples and tear ridges; MDI coating panel is streaked

OBS/morphology/feature_metric.definition: A measured metric of imaged features: size or size distribution, number density, thickness, area fraction, porosity, lattice-fringe spacing, boundary fractions by misorientation class (also when shown as a histogram of image-derived values)

OBS/morphology/distribution.definition: Spatial arrangement of features or elements across the field: uniformity, clustering, alignment, segregation, gradients
OBS/morphology/distribution.example: Dark SiC particles spread across the matrix with local clustering

STR.definition: A claim about the material's structure at any scale, inferred from observations

STR/phase/identity.definition: Which phases or crystal structures are present, including 'no secondary phase' and mesoscale periodic arrangements (colloidal crystals, block-copolymer mesophases, superlattices; attrs.scale=mesoscale)
STR/phase/identity.example: Cr-doped samples keep the misfit-layer structure; beta-Ti (bcc) forms within 30 ns

STR/phase/fraction.definition: How much of a phase is present, including its evolution with time or condition: phase fraction, degree of transformation, crystallinity of a semicrystalline polymer. When the evidence is a proxy (KAM/GAM for transformed fraction, hardness for precipitate fraction) name it in attrs.proxy; basis stays evidenced
STR/phase/fraction.example: Transformation completes in 200-300 ns near Tm

STR/phase/lattice.definition: Unit-cell dimensions, interlayer spacing or lattice strain and their change
STR/phase/lattice.example: Layer spacing c shrinks linearly from 16.97 to 16.68 A with Cr

STR/phase/site_occupancy.definition: How constituents are distributed over the crystallographic sites of a phase: which sublattice/site a species occupies and in what proportion (site preference, inversion degree, antisites), and whether a sublattice is ordered or random (order-disorder, superstructure, configurational/high-entropy disorder). Aspect (preference | ordering) and sublattice in attrs. Boundary: charge state, compensation, vacancies and dilute-defect carrier/diffusion arguments stay STR/defect/point
STR/phase/site_occupancy.example: Fe3+ takes octahedral sites, confining Co2+ to tetrahedral sites; five rare earths randomly occupy the pyrochlore A site

STR/chemistry/bonding.definition: Which bonds, functional groups, linkages or coordination are present or converted, up to a full molecular/repeat-unit structure, including molecular configuration or conformation (cis/trans isomer state, ring-open/closed photoswitch, chain conformation; attrs.aspect=configuration). Scope in attrs
STR/chemistry/bonding.example: Oil double bonds converted to oxirane rings; azobenzene cross-links isomerise trans to cis under 365 nm

STR/chemistry/composition.definition: WHAT a phase or region is made of: elemental composition, stoichiometry, oxidation/valence state, solute content, per-layer or per-particle composition. Boundary: WHERE elements are (homogeneity, segregation, gradients across the field) is STR/microstructure/distribution
STR/chemistry/composition.example: Reaction layer II is Co/Ni-rich Al(Co,Ni)2Ti; surface Ce is mixed Ce3+/Ce4+

STR/defect/point.definition: Substitutional, interstitial or vacancy species described by charge state, compensation or position (incl. the position of individual dopant atoms, attrs.aspect=position); drives carrier, ionic, diffusion and single-atom-manipulation arguments. Which-site/ordering claims over a phase without a charge or carrier argument are STR/phase/site_occupancy. In computation papers the defect may be imposed by model construction (attrs.basis=imposed)
STR/defect/point.example: Cr3+ substitutes Ti4+ as an acceptor-type defect

STR/defect/extended.definition: Line and planar defects (dislocations, stacking faults, twins, antiphase boundaries) and their density; drives mechanical and phonon arguments
STR/defect/extended.example: Higher Cr levels remove planar stacking faults

STR/microstructure.definition: Arrangement of grains, particles, pores and phases at meso/micro scale

STR/microstructure/feature_size.definition: Size of structural units (grains, particles, crystallites, pores, layers); refine/coarsen as attrs.direction
STR/microstructure/feature_size.example: Matrix grains refined from 65 to 22 um, saturating above 10 wt% SiCp

STR/microstructure/distribution.definition: Spatial distribution/homogeneity of a constituent: dispersion, agglomeration, segregation, gradient
STR/microstructure/distribution.example: Near-uniform SiCp distribution with few agglomerates

STR/microstructure/shape.definition: Shape and surface topography of structural units or of a built architecture (lenticular, acicular, equiaxed, lamellar, strut network, channel lattice, ridges, facets, roughness)
STR/microstructure/shape.example: Lens-shaped beta grains, about one nucleus per alpha grain

STR/microstructure/porosity.definition: Amount, connectivity and hierarchy of porosity: pore/void volume fraction, relative density, open vs closed, interconnection, multi-level pore systems, gel/polymer network mesh, unintended processing voids, specific surface area. Pore SIZE stays STR/microstructure/feature_size; load- or environment-induced cracks and voids are STR/microstructure/damage. Next: a transport/ingrowth argument or a correction/qualification of property values measured on porous bodies
STR/microstructure/porosity.example: Ceramics remain 20-29% porous after 1500 C sintering; designed global channels plus interconnected local pores

STR/microstructure/orientation.definition: Orientation state of a polycrystal or oriented solid: crystallographic texture / preferred orientation (films, bulk), molecular or fibre orientation in polymers, and grain-boundary character (misorientation distribution, LAGB/HAGB/twin-boundary fractions). Component, strength and direction in attrs. Next: anisotropy, slip/twin activation, recrystallisation diagnosis
STR/microstructure/orientation.example: Electropulsing weakens the basal texture and raises the HAGB fraction from 65 to 90%

STR/microstructure/damage.definition: Loss of continuity induced in a made material by load, thermal cycling or environment: microcracks and crack networks, comb/wing cracks, gouge or debris bands, delamination, fibre or particle fracture, degradation-opened cracks, damage-induced voids. Density, orientation, width and extent in attrs. Next: a frictional/Coulomb or fracture-mechanics argument, a failure-mode classification (PRP/behavior_class), or a stiffness, strength or permeability loss. Boundaries: crystallographic line/planar defects are STR/defect/extended; designed or processing pores are STR/microstructure/porosity
STR/microstructure/damage.example: Low-confinement fault: gouge of loose debris flanked by comb cracks, damage zone 2-3 grains wide

STR/interface.definition: State of an interface or boundary between constituents or with a substrate: bonding, reaction layer, coherency, wetting, adhesion

PRP.definition: A claim about a property of the material, or of an assembly (joint, coating-substrate system, electrode, device) with attrs.object. attrs.property_family is required (mechanical | thermal | thermodynamic | electrical | ionic_electrochemical | catalytic | magnetic | optical | chemical_corrosion | kinetic | biological | surface). attrs.basis=argued when no measurement supports it. Biological boundary: in-vitro cell response to the material against a design variable is PRP (biological); in-vivo endpoints and host-tissue markers are not properties of the material (see PRF/service_capability and MEC/pathway)

PRP/value.definition: The level of a property or its change with a design variable or condition (strength, conductivity, Tg, creep rate, transformation rate, threshold stress). Quantity, direction and family in attrs
PRP/value.example: Tensile yield strength increases with SiCp; UTS does not

PRP/behavior_class.definition: A categorical classification of how the material behaves: failure mode, conduction type (metallic, n-type), magnetic order, degradation mode
PRP/behavior_class.example: Mixed ductile-brittle fracture, brittle fraction growing with SiCp

PRP/descriptor.definition: A microscopic descriptor that sits between structure and a measured property as intermediate cause: carrier density, mobility, effective mass, diffusivity, defect concentration
PRP/descriptor.example: Effective mass increases with Cr, adding to the Seebeck gain

PRP/diagnostic.definition: A quantity whose main role is to identify a mechanism via a known mapping (stress exponent, activation energy, Avrami exponent, Tafel slope, mobility exponent). Next step: KNW/lookup -> MEC/identification

PRP/partition.definition: Claim that a total property is dominated by one of its contributions
PRP/partition.example: Reduction of total thermal conductivity is dominated by the electronic part

PRF.definition: A claim about performance in a use condition or device

PRF/figure_of_merit.definition: A composite application metric combining several properties (ZT, energy density, specific strength, figure of merit)
PRF/figure_of_merit.example: ZT at 750 K rises from 0.24 to 0.29

PRF/service_capability.definition: The material, device or method performs (or fails) under a stated service or use condition (temperature, load, environment, cycles, lifetime), or a built prototype or process demonstrably does the job (print, grating, sensor on tissue, deterministic atom manipulation) with demonstration conditions in attrs. Includes in-vivo application endpoints and host-tissue markers that measure endpoint quality (wound closure, histology scores, collagen deposition, bone ingrowth); host biomarkers invoked to explain the endpoint (oxidative stress, inflammation) are MEC/pathway
PRF/service_capability.example: Improved creep resistance at 175 C and 80-120 MPa for >=15 wt% SiCp; full-colour prints with 200 nm pixels written in one exposure

PRF/qualification.definition: Performance judged against standard, benchmark-condition or application test criteria (pass/fail, rating, spec, community benchmark such as overpotential at 10 mA/cm2). Boundary: a value ranked at a community benchmark condition is PRF/qualification; the same quantity argued from structure as a trend is PRP/value
PRF/qualification.example: Coatings meet hardness, gloss, adhesion and chemical-resistance requirements

MEC.definition: A mechanistic explanation linking cause to effect. The physical class (nucleation, strengthening, scattering, defect chemistry, electronic structure, ...) goes in attrs.mechanism_class; the spine link it bridges is given by its edges

MEC/pathway.definition: A causal pathway by which a cause produces an effect. attrs.basis = evidenced | argued | attributed (attribution without a pathway)
MEC/pathway.example: SiC particles act as heterogeneous nucleation sites and restrict grain growth

MEC/identification.definition: The operative mechanism is identified as one member of a known catalogue (rate-controlling step, transformation mode, scattering regime), usually via a diagnostic and a lookup; alternatives are implicitly ruled out
MEC/identification.example: Creep is climb-controlled; the alpha-beta transformation is isothermal martensitic

MEC/tradeoff.definition: A net outcome explained by one contribution outweighing an opposing one; carries counteracts edges
MEC/tradeoff.example: Lower total thermal conductivity outweighs the power-factor loss, so ZT rises

KNW.definition: Prior knowledge, literature or theory brought in as a premise

KNW/precedent.definition: A specific earlier result (own or others') used as analogy, support or comparator
KNW/precedent.example: Isothermal martensite in Fe-Ni shows S-shaped autocatalytic kinetics

KNW/model.definition: A named model, formalism or governing equation used to compute, fit or predict
KNW/model.example: Threshold-stress formalism; Wiedemann-Franz law; Pati-Cohen kinetics

KNW/lookup.definition: A known mapping from an observable value or feature to its interpretation: diagnostic value -> mechanism, band/peak position -> group or phase, reference card
KNW/lookup.example: n_t ~ 5 indicates lattice-diffusion-controlled climb; 1730 cm-1 is urethane C=O

KNW/fact.definition: A tabulated fact or known structure of a constituent used as a premise (constant, radius, composition, crystal-structure model)
KNW/fact.example: SiC compressive strength 3900 MPa; host is a BiS/TiS2 natural superlattice

DSC.definition: Discussion: generalisation, comparison to prior work, limitation, outlook

DSC/conclusion.definition: Summary claim of what was shown and what is new
DSC/conclusion.example: Cr doping optimises carrier concentration and, unlike other acceptors, raises m*

DSC/comparison.definition: Results set against prior work, a model prediction or an incumbent; attrs.against = prior_work | model | baseline and attrs.verdict
DSC/comparison.example: Models agree above 1400 K but overestimate Ea by 50% at 1200 K

DSC/design_guidance.definition: A generalised design rule, optimum window or trade-off recommendation drawn from the results
DSC/design_guidance.example: <=10 wt% SiCp suffices for strength; creep benefit needs >=15 wt%

DSC/limitation.definition: A stated limit of method or data, or an anomaly attributed to artefact, that bounds a claim (kind in attrs: method | anomaly | scope)
DSC/limitation.example: beta < 10% undetectable; the 1575 K outlier attributed to laser misalignment

DSC/outlook.definition: Proposed application or next experiment (attrs.kind = application | research)
DSC/outlook.example: Suitable for floor-care and decorative coatings; high-resolution imaging needed

rels.motivates: HYP/DSC/OBS gives reason for a DES/PRC choice or a test; a weighed claim (PRP/PRF/MEC, e.g. a trade-off or ranking) may motivate a DES/down_select (screen-then-choose)
rels.realizes: a DES choice is carried out by a PRC act or a measurement; in computation-first papers also by constructing an in-silico structure, in which case dst may be a STR node with attrs.basis=imposed; a spine DES/method whose measurement is a headline contribution may realize the STR/PRP/MEC claim it makes measurable
rels.feeds_into: src PRC act's product is the workpiece, precursor, mold or template of dst PRC act (ordered multi-step route). PRC->PRC only; replaces realizes/premise_for between PRC nodes
rels.produces: a PRC act or condition yields a structural state
rels.evidences: an OBS supports a claim (STR/PRP/PRF/MEC) or a DSC/comparison or DSC/limitation verdict. Source must be OBS
rels.causes: physical causation in the material: one state leads to another (processing -> structure -> property -> performance). Not for claim-to-conclusion reasoning
rels.explains: a MEC accounts for a claim
rels.premise_for: a KNW node, or an in-paper node used as an input, supplies an assumption, equation, parameter or condition value for another inference or derivation (absorbs proposed 'parameterizes')
rels.contrasts: a claim or OBS is compared against a control, baseline, model or alternative
rels.rules_out: evidence or reasoning rejects an alternative explanation
rels.derives: dst OBS is computed from src OBS by arithmetic, data reduction, fitting or re-plotting; dst is NOT independent evidence (absorbs proposed 'reduces_to'). Carries an mm_op when src has a figure
rels.qualifies: a limitation, caveat or anomaly bounds the scope or confidence of a claim without refuting it
rels.counteracts: src effect opposes the outcome dst stands for (the loss term of a trade-off)
rels.supports: a claim is used as a premise for another claim or conclusion (claim -> claim or claim -> DSC reasoning), as opposed to physical causation (causes) or direct measurement (evidences)

modality_notes.diffraction_pattern: Intensity vs scattering angle/vector, 1D (XRD trace, radial profile) or 2D (SAED, detector image)
modality_notes.spectrum: Intensity vs energy/wavenumber/shift/binding energy (IR, Raman, XPS, NMR, UV-vis, EDS spectrum, XAS), and real-space radial functions (FT-EXAFS, PDF); computed DOS/pDOS/COOP curves
modality_notes.xy_curve: Any quantitative plot of a quantity vs a variable or category: line, scatter, bar/histogram (incl. histograms of image-derived values), log-log, contour of a response. Not for 1D diffraction traces, spectra, line scans or dispersion diagrams
modality_notes.spatial_map: Map of a quantity or element over sample space in 2D (EDS/EBSD/EPMA map, strain map, tomogram slice, property map of hardness/modulus/conductivity) or 1D (EDS/EPMA line scan vs distance, intensity line profile across an image)
modality_notes.photograph: Macroscopic camera image of samples or devices
modality_notes.schematic: Drawn diagram, reaction scheme or structure model
modality_notes.simulation_render: Rendered simulation output (atomistic snapshot, FEM field)
modality_notes.text_only: Readout stated in text with no figure in the packet
modality_notes.composite_rule: For multi-panel figures use the modality of the panel actually read; if a node reads two panel kinds, split the node
modality_notes.volume_render: 3D surface or volume rendering of experimental tomographic or serial-section data (micro-CT, FIB-SEM, electron tomography, atom-probe reconstruction), often cut away or colour-segmented; segmentation/smoothing artefacts apply. Simulated 3D output stays simulation_render
modality_notes.orientation_distribution: Intensity over orientation space, not physical space: pole figures, inverse-pole-figure density plots, ODF sections. An EBSD IPF-coloured map is spatial_map
modality_notes.dispersion_diagram: Energy or frequency vs wavevector along a high-symmetry path: electronic band structure, phonon or magnon dispersion. The DOS panel beside it is spectrum

values.measured: directly recorded by an instrument or test
values.derived: computed in this paper from other OBS (must have an incoming derives edge)
values.computed: output of simulation, theory or model calculation (DFT, FEM, CALPHAD, analytic model)

values.shown: the figure visibly shows the claim as stated
values.partial: the figure supports a weaker, qualified or subset version (some panels/samples, within noise, low magnification)
values.not_shown: the figure does not resolve the claimed feature; the claim rests on text or tables
values.contradicts: the figure shows something inconsistent with the stated claim

image_support.note: Record what the image shows instead in attrs.image_note. Things the figure shows that the text never states become their own OBS node with attrs.text_silent=true. An audit OBS node whose label states the discrepancy itself has image_support=shown (the figure shows the discrepancy); the conflict is carried by its qualifies/contrasts edge

values.true: node lies on the paper's primary line of argument (HYP -> DES -> PRC -> STR -> PRP -> PRF -> DSC/conclusion, with bridging MEC)
values.false: evidence, premise, audit or side branch

spine.note: See PROTOCOL.md 'Spine and periphery'. OBS and KNW nodes are never spine; 10-20 spine nodes per paper. From v03: at most two parallel branches plus one control branch that ends in a PRP/STR linked by contrasts to the main branch; DES/method may be spine when the method is a headline contribution (link by realizes to the claim it makes measurable); DES/down_select is reached by motivates from the weighed claim

basis.applies_to: attrs.basis on STR/PRP/PRF/MEC claims (optional; default evidenced)

values.evidenced: supported by incoming evidences edges in this paper
values.argued: reasoned from other claims or literature, no direct measurement (e.g. dislocation density inferred from incomplete DRX)
values.attributed: asserted cause without a pathway or evidence
values.imposed: set by model construction in a computation (e.g. substitutional N placed in a DFT cell)

basis.note: Evidence through a proxy (KAM for transformed fraction, colour for dose) is still evidenced; name the proxy in attrs.proxy

mm_op_families.read: extract a feature from one figure
mm_op_families.compare: set two or more traces/panels/sources against each other
mm_op_families.match: map figure content to a reference, label or known class
mm_op_families.quantify: turn figure content into numbers or parameters
mm_op_families.transform: turn a figure into new data (on derives edges)

read_trend.definition: Read the direction, monotonicity, saturation or ranking of a quantity across an ordered series or along an axis, including crossings of overlaid curves

read_characteristic_point.definition: Read a defined point from a curve or scan: onset, peak, minimum, inflection/step (incl. via derivative curve), threshold crossing, value at a stated condition

read_distribution_statistics.definition: Read range, central value, width, tails, per-class offsets or overlap from a histogram or distribution of a non-imaged quantity over an ensemble (computed sites/configurations, specimens, light-scattering size classes). Failure modes: few counts per class, binning, indistinguishable colour classes, intensity vs number weighting

inspect_local_feature.definition: Judge a local feature (interface, defect, grain shape) in one high-magnification view; representativeness is an assumption

assess_spatial_distribution.definition: Judge uniformity, clustering, alignment or segregation of features or elements across a field of view or map

compare_across_conditions.definition: Compare panels, frames, photographs or curves that differ in one condition (design variable, stage, time, before/after) and read the difference

track_feature_across_series.definition: Follow one identified feature or object through an ordered sequence and read its shift, displacement, appearance or disappearance: a spectral/diffraction feature through stacked traces, or an imaged/simulated object (atom, particle, crack tip, domain wall, ion) through time-lapse or trajectory frames. Failure modes: object identity between frames, frame-interval aliasing (sequential vs simultaneous events)

compare_coplotted_quantities.definition: Read two or more different quantities, species or components on shared axes and judge either relative magnitude/dominance (total vs components, divergent response) or positional coincidence/overlap of their features (emission vs absorption, band vs stopband or resonance, edge vs source spectrum; attrs.aspect=overlap). Audit for overlap: judge bandwidths, not only peak coincidence

compare_with_reference_value.definition: Position this work's data against reference values plotted, tabulated or quoted alongside: prior-work points, incumbent values, experimental constants, or an in-paper benchmark system of known class

correlate_across_series.definition: Align the same sample series across two or more figures or panels with different ordinates and judge whether two different quantities co-vary (shared ranking, optimum or turnover); licenses a correlational attribution only, weaker than an intervention

register_colocated_views.definition: Register two or more views of the SAME region (different modalities or channels: image + EDS/EPMA map, line scan, point analysis, SAED at marked positions; or different magnifications) so that content read in one is located on a feature delineated in the other; failure modes are misregistration, probe size vs feature size and non-representative fields; also a photograph or map that places sensors, probes or indents on the specimen registered to the signal traces or values they recorded

match_to_reference.definition: Overlay or compare a whole pattern/spectrum with a reference trace (parent, standard, database, simulation) and judge coincidence

match_to_design.definition: Compare an image of a fabricated object or structure with its intended geometry (CAD/STL/image-based design, mold, template, target dimension) and judge fidelity: shape, dimensions, connectivity, replicated template features or defects

assign_features.definition: Assign individual peaks, reflections, bands, signals, steps, or image contrast levels/regions (Z-, mass-thickness, phase contrast) to phases, groups, sites or processes via a known mapping; includes reading which reflections/poles of two phases are parallel in a superposed pattern (orientation relationship, habit plane; attrs.aspect=orientation_relationship), which then evidences STR/interface

recognize_signature.definition: Match a visible morphology or a curve shape to a known class that implies a mechanism (dimples -> ductile; lenticular -> martensitic; sigmoid, C-curve, power law)

measure_feature_metric.definition: Measure sizes, counts, number densities, thicknesses, area or boundary fractions of imaged features, directly in the image or from a histogram of image-derived values

quantify_from_intensity.definition: Convert peak intensities, areas or widths into amounts (phase fraction, conversion, crystallite size)

quantify_from_position.definition: Convert feature positions (2theta, d-spacing, fringe or band/edge energy) into a physical parameter via a known relation: Bragg/cell refinement -> lattice parameter or strain, position -> composition via Vegard

convert_via_calibration.definition: Convert a readout (colour/hue, signal amplitude, voltage, intensity) into a physical quantity by inverting a calibration that the paper itself established on standards or a response series (colour->height, voltage->modulus, thickness->dose). Used on derives edges from the raw readout and premise_for edges from the calibration OBS. Audit: target inside the calibrated range, calibration made on a comparable substrate/state, monotone (unique) inversion

extract_slope.definition: Read the slope, intercept or exponent of a line on linearised axes (log-log, Arrhenius, Tauc) or an annotated power-law fit

fit_model.definition: Fit a model or analytic expression to a curve to obtain parameters or a reusable functional form

subtract_reference.definition: Subtract a background or reference-state trace/pattern to isolate a new component (difference pattern, baseline correction)

replot_derived_series.definition: Build a new series or diagram from other readouts: combine series arithmetically (e.g. S^2*sigma, kappa - kappa_e), aggregate snapshots/samples, resample curves at iso-levels, re-plot against another variable

overlay_model_on_data.definition: Overlay a model prediction or fit on data and judge agreement region by region

collapse_by_normalization.definition: Re-plot against a normalised/corrected variable and check whether curves from different conditions merge; the merge is the evidence

flag_outlier.definition: Identify a point or series deviating from the trend of the others and set it aside or explain it

cross_check_consistency.definition: Verify that quantities read from different figures/panels agree arithmetically or in trend (e.g. total minus component equals plotted component)

changelog: Types 80 -> 82 (+2 leaves): STR/microstructure/damage (S1; ice faults, degradation cracks), OBS/response/distribution (S3; ensemble spread, DLS)
No renames of types; OBS/signal/feature_shift broadened to position relative to another species' feature (aspect=overlap) instead of a new leaf

Boundary rules written into definitions: forming (feedstock -> body, incl. patterning and in-situ gelation) vs treatment (working a made body incl. hot extrusion of billets; powder milling/classification); reactive consolidation = one synthesis node with concurrent_forming; self-assembly in dispersion = synthesis, on a substrate = deposition

Biological boundary: in-vitro cell response = PRP (biological); in-vivo endpoints and endpoint-quality tissue markers = PRF/service_capability; explanatory host biomarkers = MEC/pathway; biodegradation = property_family chemical_corrosion

PRF/service_capability covers demonstrations of prototypes and process capability; STR/phase/identity covers mesoscale periodic lattices; STR/phase/fraction covers polymer crystallinity and proxies; STR/chemistry/bonding covers isomer/configuration; STR/defect/point covers single-dopant position; porosity covers gel network mesh
Rels: motivates may run claim -> DES/down_select; realizes may run spine DES/method -> the claim it makes measurable

mm_ops 25 -> 27: +read_distribution_statistics (read), +convert_via_calibration (quantify); assess_feature_overlap merged into compare_coplotted_quantities (aspect=overlap); read_orientation_relationship merged into assign_features (aspect=orientation_relationship); track_feature_across_series broadened to object tracking in frame sequences; register_colocated_views covers sensor/probe/indent position photographs
Modality note: property maps and intensity line profiles across images are spatial_map; spine note allows one control branch and headline DES/method
Merge phase opened: usage block gives r01-r03 counts after renames; candidates listed in rounds/r03/judge.md

property_family_notes.catalytic: activity/selectivity of a catalyst: electro-, photo-, thermocatalytic (OER overpotential, dye-degradation rate)
property_family_notes.thermodynamic: formation, binding, cohesive, surface or interfacial energies and phase stability
property_family_notes.ionic_electrochemical: ionic conduction, redox capacity, battery/supercapacitor behaviour; not catalytic activity
property_family_notes.chemical_corrosion: corrosion, oxidation, chemical resistance, degradation in environment, including hydrolytic, enzymatic and in-body biodegradation (Mg implant corrosion, polymer hydrolysis, scaffold mass loss)
property_family_notes.biological: in-vitro response of cells, bacteria or proteins to the material (viability, adhesion, proliferation, antibacterial activity, haemolysis); in-vivo endpoints are PRF/service_capability

usage.scope: r01-r03 graphs (28 papers), node/edge counts after v01-v03 renames; [count, papers]
